signals.title: USD/CAD — G10 Outperformance + NFP Shock + Jobs Double Surprise
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3938 following a high-impact divergence in North American labor data. The US Dollar Index tumbled to a 7-week low after a disappointing July NFP report triggered a sharp trimming of Fed hike bets, while Canadian jobs data delivered a 'double surprise' to the upside. This fundamental shock has pushed USD/CAD below its SMA20/50 cluster at 1.4066/1.4068, shifting the technical posture to bearish. CAD ESI sits at +12.0 compared to the USD ESI of -6.4, confirming that Canadian data is consistently outperforming expectations while US data misses. Despite a 150bp nominal carry advantage favoring the USD, the real rate differential is narrower (USD +1.56% vs CAD +0.16%), making the USD vulnerable to this growth-driven repricing. Risk: A rapid reversal in WTI oil prices toward $70/bbl provides an offset that stabilizes the pair despite the labor data divergence.

signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hormuz Risk
signals.text: CHF/JPY is the primary locus of G10 volatility as JPY outperformance (avg +1.240%) collides with CHF weakness (avg -0.730%), creating a massive 1.970% G10 spread. JPY is currently the strongest currency in the G10 complex, supported by a positive ESI of +16.1 and a bull-steepening US yield curve that typically signals recessionary pricing. While JPY usually acts as a safe haven, the z-score of +1.39σ for its correlation with VIX suggests its traditional function is under pressure, replaced by carry-unwind dynamics as the USD/JPY carry of 275bp remains high. Geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and the US-Iran war headline provide a floor for JPY demand despite its -100bp carry disadvantage against CHF. Risk: De-escalation in Middle East negotiations leads to a sharp JPY carry-reinstatement, reversing the weekly trend.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options Skew + Bull Steepener
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.84 is testing the SMA200 at 158.05 from below after the US NFP shock triggered a bull steepener in the US curve (2s10s +46.7bp). Options markets are aggressively pricing downside protection, with 1M 25d Risk Reversals at -2.20, a strong put skew that signals institutional fear of a deeper correction. This skew exists despite a negative Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of -1.1%, suggesting that while the options market is 'complacent' regarding realized volatility, it is paying a premium for directional JPY strength. COT data shows specs remain net short JPY (lev_net -124,575), leaving the pair highly susceptible to a squeeze if US yields continue to soften. Risk: BoJ holds its neutral stance at the next meeting, allowing the 275bp OIS carry advantage to re-assert dominance over the pair.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5887, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5829/0.5791). An active divergence exists between speculative positioning and central bank fundamentals; COT LF net is short -30,606 (only 9.7% long) while the RBNZ is in an active HIKING cycle with a positive ESI of +24.4. This creates an asymmetric short-squeeze setup where specs are fading the G10's strongest data performer. Although the USD maintains a +125bp nominal carry lead, the NZD real rate of -1.56% vs USD +1.56% shows the RBNZ is still accommodative relative to inflation, providing a long-term catalyst for further hikes. Risk: A broader risk-off move in equities (S&P 500 < 7,500) triggers a liquidation of pro-cyclical NZD positions, validating the spec short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7063, positioned above all major daily SMAs (20/50/200). The options market is pricing in significant tail risk with a VRP of +3.1% (IV 9.2% vs HV30 6.1%), indicating that traders are paying up for protection as the RBA meeting on 11 August approaches. Retail sentiment is currently 75% short, diverging from the COT LF net long of +23,616. This institutional vs retail divergence at the top of the range suggests retail traders are unsuccessfully trying to fade the AUD's 60bp OIS carry advantage. Sustained price action above 0.7100 would likely force retail capitulation and fuel a further move higher. Risk: RBA adopts a surprisingly dovish tone on 11 August, removing the carry support and allowing the retail short bias to finally profit.
